items.explanation: ザ is 'za': サ ('sa') with dakuten. It is the same sound as hiragana ざ. The two small ticks ゛ are called dakuten. They make the consonant voiced, meaning your vocal cords buzz: k becomes g, s becomes z, t becomes d, and h becomes b. Touch your throat while saying 'k' and then 'g' to feel the difference.
items.mnemonic: サ plus two ticks for buzzing vocal cords: 'sa' starts to buzz and becomes 'za'.

items.explanation: ジ is 'ji': シ ('shi') with dakuten. It is the same sound as hiragana じ. It sounds like the 'j' in 'jeep', not 'zee'. Both 'ji' and 'zi' are accepted.
items.mnemonic: シ plus two ticks for buzzing vocal cords: 'shi' starts to buzz and becomes 'ji'.

items.explanation: ズ is 'zu': ス ('su') with dakuten. It is the same sound as hiragana ず. Many speakers say it with a light 'dz' at the start of a word.
items.mnemonic: ス plus two ticks for buzzing vocal cords: 'su' starts to buzz and becomes 'zu'.

items.explanation: ゼ is 'ze': セ ('se') with dakuten. It is the same sound as hiragana ぜ.
items.mnemonic: セ plus two ticks for buzzing vocal cords: 'se' starts to buzz and becomes 'ze'.

items.explanation: ゾ is 'zo': ソ ('so') with dakuten. It is the same sound as hiragana ぞ.
items.mnemonic: ソ plus two ticks for buzzing vocal cords: 'so' starts to buzz and becomes 'zo'.
